title: Refrigerant and ozone layer / Unit 8 key points

paras.text: property of damaging the ozone layer. Modern refrigerators usually use a refrigerant called hydrofluorocarbon (HFC), which was supposed to have zero potential to deplete the ozone layer. However in 1974 researchers predicted that emissions of HFCs could damage Earth's atmosphere by the catalytic destruction of ozone in the stratosphere. The hypothesis has been proven in 1985 by measurements which have shown the destruction of the ozone layer over Antarctica. Scientists are now looking to develop new refrigerant that is natural and have low global warming potential (GWP) and zero Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP).

paras.text: Editorial note: the textbook attributes the 1974 ozone prediction to HFCs; historically the 1974 prediction and the 1985 Antarctic measurements concerned CFCs.
